v0.8-specific cooperative-interposition acceptance includes:
  - standalone Alchemy retains the historical direct object wrapper
  - an already-active generic coordinator is detected structurally
  - Alchemy registers provider ALCHEMY.EXECUTION_PROVENANCE at priority 1000
  - coordinator-first operation retains exactly one physical wrapper while two providers observe the call
  - Alchemy can withdraw its coordinated provider without disabling the other provider
  - public cooperative callbacks reject a forged call lacking the opaque per-object token
  - alchemyBaseState reports cooperative protocol availability and coordinated instrumentation count without disclosing token/interceptor objects
  - sealed introspection includes alchemy.objects.method-interposition/0.1 structural evidence
  - INSTRUMENTMETHOD, INSTRUMENTREGISTEREDMETHODS and UNINSTRUMENTMETHOD are PROTECTED
  - hosted Security Manager policy can deny customer instrumentation installation/removal without mutating the object
  - a direct Alchemy layer refuses unsafe removal while an outer coordinator owns the current method

Actual ooRexx Logging v0.3 integration result: 3/3 PASS.
  Logging package regression unchanged:
    PASS test_alchemy_preexisting_telemetry

    PASS test_logging_first_alchemy
    PASS test_alchemy_first_remove_while_logging

The Logging integration confirms both installation orders and fail-safe release order against the supplied oorexx_logging_v0.3 package, while the core Alchemy runtime retains no Logging dependency.

Inspector boundary additions:
  - AlchemyInspectorBridge does not follow or emit ALCHEMYINTERPOSITIONTOKEN
  - AlchemyInspectorBridge does not follow or emit ALCHEMYINTERPOSITIONINTERCEPTOR
  - AlchemyInspectorBridge does not follow external __MISLOTS coordinator state
  - existing sealer/capability-authority/locked-vault suppressions remain intact

Known platform evidence carried forward, not re-labelled as v0.8 field validation:
  - project-host ooRexx 5.2.0 r0 completed the 22-test v0.4.3 suite uninterrupted in 15.940s
  - that run independently reproduced the static ::REQUIRES Security Manager supervision gap
  - v0.8 requires its own field rerun before claiming release-level 5.2.0 validation

Important scope/limitations:
  - cooperative interposition is an instrumentation compatibility protocol, not an authority source
  - a host must trust the active coordinator implementation before treating coordinated telemetry as high-assurance provenance
  - automatic instrumentation still refuses PROTECTED, PRIVATE, PACKAGE-scope and reserved AlchemyObject methods
  - execution history remains bounded and dropped/evicted evidence is counted rather than hidden
  - abrupt interpreter/process termination can leave a retained execution record incomplete
  - static ::REQUIRES remains outside the observed per-routine Security Manager checkpoint path on the validated platform lineage
